title: Cap. X Arg. VI: therefore God’s will predominates — Cain/Judas/Hymenaeus vs Peter/Paul; reprobation’s non-gift of faith precedes foreseen unbelief
pass_a_gloss: We must therefore at length return hither, that we confess that with God is the principal determination of things future and not-future; inasmuch as in good acts he has decreed to apply his efficacious operation unto producing them; inasmuch as in evils which are produced by wicked men, he has decreed by no means to hinder them; finally, inasmuch as in good acts which would be omitted by the same, he has decreed not to give the efficacious grace by which they would be done. And thus the will of God is the predominating and predetermining cause as to the non-being of things by no means future, because although he can make them future if he wills, yet he does not will to do this which he could. Now truly not to will from eternity to do, when he could, that Cain should repent, that Judas should believe, that Hymenaeus should persevere, is a firm demonstration of antecedent non-election; just as to will to effect that Peter should repent, that Paul should believe and persevere, is a clear proof of antecedent election. But this decree of reprobation, which contains the determined act of the Divine will concerning faith, repentance, perseverance not to be given unto certain persons, must of necessity precede their unbelief, impenitence, both foreseen and certainly future.
pass_b_english: So we must come back to this: with God lies the principal determination of futures and non-futures—in good acts, by decreeing to apply his efficacious operation to produce them; in evils produced by the wicked, by decreeing not to hinder them; and in good acts those same would omit, by decreeing not to give the efficacious grace by which they would be done. Thus God’s will is the predominating, predetermining cause of the non-being of things that will not be: he can make them future if he wills, yet he does not will to do what he could. Not willing from eternity—though he could—that Cain repent, Judas believe, Hymenaeus persevere, firmly demonstrates antecedent non-election; willing to bring about that Peter repent, Paul believe and persevere, clearly proves antecedent election. And this reprobation decree—the determined act of the divine will not to give faith, repentance, perseverance to certain persons—must precede their unbelief and impenitence, foreseen and certainly future.
source_text: Eo igitur tandem redeundum est, ut fateamur penes Deum esse principalem rerum futurarum et non-futurarum determinationem; quatenus in bonis actibus decrevit ad eos producendos efficacem suam operationem adhibere; quatenus in malis, quae ab hominibus improbis producuntur, decrevit eos minime impedire; denique, quatenus in bonis actibus, qui ab iisdem omitterentur, decrevit non dare gratiam efficacem qua fierent. Et sic voluntas Dei est causa predominans et praedeterminans quoad non-esse rerum minime futurarum, quoniam cum possit facere ut essent futurae si vellet, non vult tamen hoc facere quod posset. Jam vero ab aeterno non velle facere cum posset, ut Cain poeniteat, ut Judas credat, ut Hymenaeus perseveret, est antecedaneae non-electionis firma demonstratio; sicut velle efficere ut Petrus poeniteat, ut Paulus credat et perseveret, est antecedaneae electionis clara probatio. Hoc autem reprobationis decretum, quod continet determinatum actum Divinae voluntatis de non danda fide, poenitentia, perseverantia certis quibusdam personis, earundem infidelitatem, impoenitentiam et praevisam et certo futuram praecedat est necesse.
